author: "Trinity Harden"

  echo: false

::: {.lead}
Exploring electoral patterns in North Carolina statewide races featuring a female candidate running against a male candidate.
:::

In North Carolina electoral history, several high-profile U.S. Senate races have featured a female candidate facing a male opponent. Most notably in **2022**, former North Carolina Supreme Court Chief Justice **Cheri Beasley** (Democrat) became the first Black woman nominated for U.S. Senate in the state, running against **Ted Budd** (Republican).

The animated map below uses `gganimate` to cycle back and forth between the **2022 woman-vs.-man matchup** and the **2026 election**, illustrating county-by-county shifts in vote margin across North Carolina.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(gganimate)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# 1. 2022 Results: Cheri Beasley (Woman / D) vs Ted Budd (Man / R)
url_2022 <- "https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/ENRS/2022_11_08/results_pct_20221108.zip"
temp22 <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
download.file(url_2022, temp22, quiet = TRUE)
raw22 <- read_tsv(unz(temp22, "results_pct_20221108.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE)

m22 <- raw22 |>
  filter(`Contest Name` == "US SENATE", Choice %in% c("Cheri Beasley", "Ted Budd")) |>
  group_by(County, Choice) |>
  summarize(votes = sum(`Total Votes`), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Choice, values_from = votes, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    total = `Cheri Beasley` + `Ted Budd`,
    dem_margin = (`Cheri Beasley` - `Ted Budd`) / total * 100,
    county_upper = toupper(County),
    election = "2022: Cheri Beasley (Woman / D) vs. Ted Budd (Man / R)"
  ) |>
  select(county_upper, election, dem_margin)

# 2. 2026 Results: Roy Cooper (Man / D) vs Michael Whatley (Man / R)
url_2026 <- "https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/ENRS/2026_11_03/results_pct_20261103.zip"
temp26 <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
download.file(url_2026, temp26, quiet = TRUE)
raw26 <- read_tsv(unz(temp26, "results_pct_20261103.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE)

m26 <- raw26 |>
  filter(`Contest Name` == "US SENATE", Choice %in% c("Roy Cooper", "Michael Whatley")) |>
  group_by(County, Choice) |>
  summarize(votes = sum(`Total Votes`), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Choice, values_from = votes, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    total = `Roy Cooper` + `Michael Whatley`,
    dem_margin = (`Roy Cooper` - `Michael Whatley`) / total * 100,
    county_upper = toupper(County),
    election = "2026: Roy Cooper (Man / D) vs. Michael Whatley (Man / R)"
  ) |>
  select(county_upper, election, dem_margin)

# 3. Combine both elections and join with NC county boundaries
combined <- bind_rows(m22, m26)

nc_counties <- counties(state = "NC", cb = TRUE, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  mutate(county_upper = toupper(NAME)) |>
  inner_join(combined, by = "county_upper")

# 4. Animated map cycling between the two elections
p <- ggplot(nc_counties) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = dem_margin), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#ca0020",
    mid = "#f7f7f7",
    high = "#0571b0",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-80, 80),
    name = "Margin (%)",
    labels = \(x) paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""), round(x), "%")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "{closest_state}",
    subtitle = "Comparing North Carolina US Senate Vote Margins",
    caption = "Source: North Carolina State Board of Elections"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray30"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  transition_states(election, transition_length = 1, state_length = 3)

animate(p, nframes = 20, fps = 4, width = 7.5, height = 4.5, units = "in", res = 100)
```
